correctness.summary: First-order circumcenter optimality supplies a positive equilibrium support of at most n+1 tangent directions. The space-form cosine laws and the equilibrium identity give the exact weighted support formula; adding and subtracting the diameter value yields the nonnegative Jung-defect decomposition and all stated sharp corollaries.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Classical Euclidean, spherical, hyperbolic and CAT(k) Jung theorems, Schneider's Minkowski/Banach-Mazur stability theorem, and Euclidean MEB duality are excluded. No located source states the unified constant-curvature defect decomposition or the sharp deficit-to-support-cardinality hierarchy. Residual risk remains from Dekster 1995, Lang-Schroeder 1997, and older MEB folklore.

value.summary: The theorem gives an exact certificate separating barycentric imbalance from active-edge shortfall and turns near equality into a sharp discrete support-dimension threshold, with simultaneous Euclidean, spherical and hyperbolic formulations.

limitations: Spherical case is restricted to the non-antipodal Jung regime.
Controls active circum-support rather than the whole set in Hausdorff or Banach-Mazur distance.
No exact extension is claimed to general CAT(k) spaces.
The Euclidean weighted support identity is not claimed as new by itself.
Originality is to the best of our knowledge; Dekster 1995 and Lang-Schroeder 1997 remain the main older-literature risks.
